title: Space Tech Briefing — July 30, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts, and welcome to your daily dose of cosmic currents! It's Thursday, July 30, 2026, and we're soaring through the latest and greatest from the final frontier. Get ready to launch into today's top stories!

First up, fresh off the launchpad, we have some incredible news from France! The CNES reports on C'Space 2026, an event that truly ignited the passion of future space engineers. From July 11th to the 18th, hundreds of young people gathered at the Ger military camp. They spent an entire week living like real space engineers, launching miniature rockets and miniature satellites! What an experience! This annual event is absolutely crucial, shaping the minds and skills of the next generation of space actors. It's truly inspiring to see.

And as we look forward to the exciting developments still on the horizon, let's take a moment to recap a major recent success that continues to reverberate across the industry. Just last week, on July 24th UTC, SpaceX achieved a monumental milestone with Starship Flight 13! This was a truly impressive test flight, confirming several major technical objectives. We saw the successful deployment of the *first* Starlink V3 satellites, a critical in-flight engine relight, and a flawless atmospheric re-entry. The mission concluded with a gentle splashdown in the Indian Ocean. This flight marked a significant step forward for the Starship program, validating those powerful Raptor V3 engines in space. It leaves us all wondering: will the 14th flight attempt an orbital mission? The anticipation is palpable!

And that's your morning briefing from the world of space technology! Thank you for joining us today. Keep your eyes on the skies, and we'll be back tomorrow with more thrilling updates. Until then, stay curious, and keep reaching for the stars!
